settings.name: layer_height
settings.label: Layer height
settings.explanation: Slicing height for each layer. Smaller layer height means more accurate and more printing time.

settings.name: initial_layer_print_height
settings.label: First layer height
settings.explanation: Height of the first layer. Making the first layer height thicker can improve build plate adhesion.

settings.name: line_width
settings.label: Default
settings.explanation: Default line width if other line widths are set to 0. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

settings.name: initial_layer_line_width
settings.label: First layer
settings.explanation: Line width of the first layer. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

settings.name: outer_wall_line_width
settings.label: Outer wall
settings.explanation: Line width of outer wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

settings.name: inner_wall_line_width
settings.label: Inner wall
settings.explanation: Line width of inner wall. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

settings.name: top_surface_line_width
settings.label: Top surface
settings.explanation: Line width for top surfaces. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

settings.name: sparse_infill_line_width
settings.label: Sparse infill
settings.explanation: Line width of internal sparse infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

settings.name: internal_solid_infill_line_width
settings.label: Internal solid infill
settings.explanation: Line width of internal solid infill. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

settings.name: support_line_width
settings.label: Support
settings.explanation: Line width of support. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.

settings.name: bridge_line_width
settings.label: Bridge
settings.explanation:
Line width of the Bridge. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over the nozzle diameter.
Recommended to use with a higher Bridge density or Bridge flow ratio.

The maximum value is 100% or the nozzle diameter.
If set to 0, the line width will match the Internal solid infill width.

settings.name: seam_position
settings.label: Seam position
settings.explanation: The start position to print each part of outer wall.

settings.name: staggered_inner_seams
settings.label: Staggered inner seams
settings.explanation: This option causes the inner seams to be shifted backwards based on their depth, forming a zigzag pattern.

settings.name: seam_gap
settings.label: Seam gap
settings.explanation:
In order to reduce the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, the loop is interrupted and shortened by a specified amount.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current extruder diameter. The default value for this parameter is 10%.

settings.name: seam_slope_type
settings.label: Scarf joint seam (beta)
settings.explanation: Use scarf joint to minimize seam visibility and increase seam strength.

settings.name: seam_slope_conditional
settings.label: Conditional scarf joint
settings.explanation: Apply scarf joints only to smooth perimeters where traditional seams do not conceal the seams at sharp corners effectively.

settings.name: scarf_angle_threshold
settings.label: Conditional angle threshold
settings.explanation:
This option sets the threshold angle for applying a conditional scarf joint seam.
If the maximum angle within the perimeter loop exceeds this value (indicating the absence of sharp corners), a scarf joint seam will be used. The default value is 155°.

settings.name: scarf_overhang_threshold
settings.label: Conditional overhang threshold
settings.explanation: This option determines the overhang threshold for the application of scarf joint seams. If the unsupported portion of the perimeter is less than this threshold, scarf joint seams will be applied. The default threshold is set at 40% of the external wall's width. Due to performance considerations, the degree of overhang is estimated.

settings.name: scarf_joint_speed
settings.label: Scarf joint speed
settings.explanation: This option sets the printing speed for scarf joints. It is recommended to print scarf joints at a slow speed (less than 100 mm/s). It's also advisable to enable 'Extrusion rate smoothing' if the set speed varies significantly from the speed of the outer or inner walls. If the speed specified here is higher than the speed of the outer or inner walls, the printer will default to the slower of the two speeds. When specified as a percentage (e.g., 80%), the speed is calculated based on the respective outer or inner wall speed. The default value is set to 100%.

settings.name: seam_slope_start_height
settings.label: Scarf start height
settings.explanation:
Start height of the scarf.
This amount can be specified in millimeters or as a percentage of the current layer height. The default value for this parameter is 0.

settings.name: seam_slope_entire_loop
settings.label: Scarf around entire wall
settings.explanation: The scarf extends to the entire length of the wall.

settings.name: seam_slope_min_length
settings.label: Scarf length
settings.explanation: Length of the scarf. Setting this parameter to zero effectively disables the scarf.

settings.name: seam_slope_steps
settings.label: Scarf steps
settings.explanation: Minimum number of segments of each scarf.

settings.name: scarf_joint_flow_ratio
settings.label: Scarf joint flow ratio
settings.explanation: This factor affects the amount of material for scarf joints.

settings.name: seam_slope_inner_walls
settings.label: Scarf joint for inner walls
settings.explanation: Use scarf joint for inner walls as well.

settings.name: role_based_wipe_speed
settings.label: Role base wipe speed
settings.explanation: The wipe speed is determined by the speed of the current extrusion role. e.g. if a wipe action is executed immediately following an outer wall extrusion, the speed of the outer wall extrusion will be utilized for the wipe action.

settings.name: wipe_speed
settings.label: Wipe speed
settings.explanation: The wipe speed is determined by the speed setting specified in this configuration. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 80%), it will be calculated based on the travel speed setting above. The default value for this parameter is 80%.

settings.name: wipe_on_loops
settings.label: Wipe on loops
settings.explanation: To minimize the visibility of the seam in a closed loop extrusion, a small inward movement is executed before the extruder leaves the loop.

settings.name: wipe_before_external_loop
settings.label: Wipe before external loop
settings.explanation:
To minimize visibility of potential overextrusion at the start of an external perimeter when printing with Outer/Inner or Inner/Outer/Inner wall print order, the de-retraction is performed slightly on the inside from the start of the external perimeter. That way any potential over extrusion is hidden from the outside surface.

This is useful when printing with Outer/Inner or Inner/Outer/Inner wall print order as in these modes it is more likely an external perimeter is printed immediately after a de-retraction move.

settings.name: slice_closing_radius
settings.label: Slice gap closing radius
settings.explanation: Cracks smaller than 2x gap closing radius are being filled during the triangle mesh slicing. The gap closing operation may reduce the final print resolution, therefore it is advisable to keep the value reasonably low.

settings.name: resolution
settings.label: Resolution
settings.explanation: The G-code path is generated after simplifying the contour of models to avoid too many points and G-code lines. Smaller value means higher resolution and more time to slice.

settings.name: enable_arc_fitting
settings.label: Arc fitting
settings.explanation:
Enable this to get a G-code file which has G2 and G3 moves. The fitting tolerance is same as the resolution.

Note: For Klipper machines, this option is recommended to be disabled. Klipper does not benefit from arc commands as these are split again into line segments by the firmware. This results in a reduction in surface quality as line segments are converted to arcs by the slicer and then back to line segments by the firmware.

settings.name: xy_hole_compensation
settings.label: X-Y hole compensation
settings.explanation: Holes in objects will expand or contract in the XY plane by the configured value. Positive values make holes bigger, negative values make holes smaller. This function is used to adjust sizes slightly when the objects have assembling issues.

settings.name: xy_contour_compensation
settings.label: X-Y contour compensation
settings.explanation: Contours of objects will expand or contract in the XY plane by the configured value. Positive values make contours bigger, negative values make contours smaller. This function is used to adjust sizes slightly when the objects have assembling issues.

settings.name: elefant_foot_compensation
settings.label: Elephant foot compensation
settings.explanation: Shrinks the first layer on build plate to compensate for elephant foot effect.

settings.name: elefant_foot_layers_density
settings.label: Elephant foot layers density
settings.explanation:
Density of internal solid infill for Elephant foot layers compensation.
The initial value for the second layer is set.
Subsequent layers become linearly denser by the height specified in elefant_foot_compensation_layers.

settings.name: elefant_foot_compensation_layers
settings.label: Elephant foot compensation layers
settings.explanation: The number of layers on which the elephant foot compensation will be active. The first layer will be shrunk by the elephant foot compensation value, then the next layers will be linearly shrunk less, up to the layer indicated by this value.

settings.name: precise_outer_wall
settings.label: Precise wall
settings.explanation: Improve shell precision by adjusting outer wall spacing. This also improves layer consistency. NOTE: This option will be ignored for outer-inner or inner-outer-inner wall sequences.

settings.name: precise_z_height
settings.label: Precise Z height
settings.explanation: Enable this to get precise Z height of object after slicing. It will get the precise object height by fine-tuning the layer heights of the last few layers. Note that this is an experimental parameter.

settings.name: hole_to_polyhole
settings.label: Convert holes to polyholes
settings.explanation:
Search for almost-circular holes that span more than one layer and convert the geometry to polyholes. Use the nozzle size and the (biggest) diameter to compute the polyhole.
See http://hydraraptor.blogspot.com/2011/02/polyholes.html

settings.name: hole_to_polyhole_threshold
settings.label: Polyhole detection margin
settings.explanation:
Maximum defection of a point to the estimated radius of the circle.
As cylinders are often exported as triangles of varying size, points may not be on the circle circumference. This setting allows you some leeway to broaden the detection.
In mm or in % of the radius.

settings.name: hole_to_polyhole_twisted
settings.label: Polyhole twist
settings.explanation: Rotate the polyhole every layer.

settings.name: ironing_type
settings.label: Ironing Type
settings.explanation: Ironing is using small flow to print on same height of surface again to make flat surface more smooth. This setting controls which layer being ironed.

settings.name: ironing_pattern
settings.label: Ironing Pattern
settings.explanation: The pattern that will be used when ironing.

settings.name: ironing_flow
settings.label: Ironing flow
settings.explanation: The amount of material to extrude during ironing. Relative to flow of normal layer height. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface.

settings.name: ironing_spacing
settings.label: Ironing line spacing
settings.explanation: The distance between the lines of ironing.

settings.name: ironing_inset
settings.label: Ironing inset
settings.explanation: The distance to keep from the edges. A value of 0 sets this to half of the nozzle diameter.

settings.name: ironing_angle
settings.label: Ironing angle offset
settings.explanation: The angle of ironing lines offset from the top surface.

settings.name: ironing_angle_fixed
settings.label: Fixed ironing angle
settings.explanation: Use a fixed absolute angle for ironing.

settings.name: zaa_enabled
settings.label: Z contouring enabled
settings.explanation: Enable Z-layer contouring (aka Z-layer anti-aliasing).

settings.name: zaa_minimize_perimeter_height
settings.label: Minimize wall height angle
settings.explanation:
Reduce the height of top-surface perimeters to match the model edge height.
Affects perimeters with a slope less than this angle (degrees).
A reasonable value is 35. Set to 0 to disable.

settings.name: zaa_min_z
settings.label: Minimum Z height
settings.explanation:
Minimum Z-layer height.
Also controls the slicing plane.

settings.name: zaa_dont_alternate_fill_direction
settings.label: Don't alternate fill direction
settings.explanation: Disable alternating fill direction when using Z contouring.

settings.name: wall_generator
settings.label: Wall generator
settings.explanation: Classic wall generator produces walls with constant extrusion width and for very thin areas is used gap-fill. Arachne engine produces walls with variable extrusion width.

settings.name: wall_transition_angle
settings.label: Wall transitioning threshold angle
settings.explanation: When to create transitions between even and odd numbers of walls. A wedge shape with an angle greater than this setting will not have transitions and no walls will be printed in the center to fill the remaining space. Reducing this setting reduces the number and length of these center walls, but may leave gaps or overextrude.

settings.name: wall_transition_filter_deviation
settings.label: Wall transitioning filter margin
settings.explanation: Prevent transitioning back and forth between one extra wall and one less. This margin extends the range of extrusion widths which follow to [Minimum wall width - margin, 2 * Minimum wall width + margin]. Increasing this margin reduces the number of transitions, which reduces the number of extrusion starts/stops and travel time. However, large extrusion width variation can lead to under- or overextrusion problems. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

settings.name: wall_transition_length
settings.label: Wall transition length
settings.explanation: When transitioning between different numbers of walls as the part becomes thinner, a certain amount of space is allotted to split or join the wall segments. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

settings.name: wall_distribution_count
settings.label: Wall distribution count
settings.explanation: The number of walls, counted from the center, over which the variation needs to be spread. Lower values mean that the outer walls don't change in width.

settings.name: initial_layer_min_bead_width
settings.label: First layer minimum wall width
settings.explanation: The minimum wall width that should be used for the first layer is recommended to be set to the same size as the nozzle. This adjustment is expected to enhance adhesion.

settings.name: min_bead_width
settings.label: Minimum wall width
settings.explanation: Width of the wall that will replace thin features (according to the Minimum feature size) of the model. If the Minimum wall width is thinner than the thickness of the feature, the wall will become as thick as the feature itself. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

settings.name: min_feature_size
settings.label: Minimum feature size
settings.explanation: Minimum thickness of thin features. Model features that are thinner than this value will not be printed, while features thicker than than this value will be widened to the minimum wall width. It's expressed as a percentage over nozzle diameter.

settings.name: min_length_factor
settings.label: Minimum wall length
settings.explanation:
Adjust this value to prevent short, unclosed walls from being printed, which could increase print time. Higher values remove more and longer walls.

NOTE: Bottom and top surfaces will not be affected by this value to prevent visual gaps on the outside of the model. Adjust 'One wall threshold' in the Advanced settings below to adjust the sensitivity of what is considered a top-surface. 'One wall threshold' is only visible if this setting is set above the default value of 0.5, or if single-wall top surfaces is enabled.

settings.name: wall_maximum_resolution
settings.label: Maximum wall resolution
settings.explanation: This value determines the smallest wall line segment length in mm. The smaller you set this value, the more accurate and precise the walls will be.

settings.name: wall_maximum_deviation
settings.label: Maximum wall deviation
settings.explanation: The maximum deviation allowed when reducing the resolution for the 'Maximum wall resolution' setting. If you increase this, the print will be less accurate, but the G-Code will be smaller. 'Maximum wall deviation' limits 'Maximum wall resolution', so if the two conflict, 'Maximum wall deviation' takes precedence.

settings.name: wall_sequence
settings.label: Walls printing order
settings.explanation:
Print sequence of the internal (inner) and external (outer) walls.

Use Inner/Outer for best overhangs. This is because the overhanging walls can adhere to a neighbouring perimeter while printing. However, this option results in slightly reduced surface quality as the external perimeter is deformed by being squashed to the internal perimeter.

Use Inner/Outer/Inner for the best external surface finish and dimensional accuracy as the external wall is printed undisturbed from an internal perimeter. However, overhang performance will reduce as there is no internal perimeter to print the external wall against. This option requires a minimum of 3 walls to be effective as it prints the internal walls from the 3rd perimeter onwards first, then the external perimeter and, finally, the first internal perimeter. This option is recommended against the Outer/Inner option in most cases.

Use Outer/Inner for the same external wall quality and dimensional accuracy benefits of Inner/Outer/Inner option. However, the Z seams will appear less consistent as the first extrusion of a new layer starts on a visible surface.

settings.name: is_infill_first
settings.label: Print infill first
settings.explanation:
Order of wall/infill. When the tickbox is unchecked the walls are printed first, which works best in most cases.

Printing infill first may help with extreme overhangs as the walls have the neighbouring infill to adhere to. However, the infill will slightly push out the printed walls where it is attached to them, resulting in a worse external surface finish. It can also cause the infill to shine through the external surfaces of the part.

settings.name: wall_direction
settings.label: Wall loop direction
settings.explanation:
The direction which the contour wall loops are extruded when looking down from the top.
Holes are printed in the opposite direction to the contour to maintain alignment with layers whose contour polygons are incomplete and change direction, also partially forming the contour of a hole.

This option will be disabled if spiral vase mode is enabled.

settings.name: print_flow_ratio
settings.label: Flow ratio
settings.explanation:
The material may have volumetric change after switching between molten and crystalline states. This setting changes all extrusion flow of this filament in G-code proportionally. The recommended value range is between 0.95 and 1.05. You may be able to tune this value to get a nice flat surface if there is slight overflow or underflow.

The final object flow ratio is this value multiplied by the filament flow ratio.

settings.name: top_solid_infill_flow_ratio
settings.label: Top surface flow ratio
settings.explanation:
This factor affects the amount of material for top solid infill. You can decrease it slightly to have smooth surface finish.

The actual top surface flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

settings.name: bottom_solid_infill_flow_ratio
settings.label: Bottom surface flow ratio
settings.explanation:
This factor affects the amount of material for bottom solid infill.

The actual bottom solid infill flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

settings.name: set_other_flow_ratios
settings.label: Set other flow ratios
settings.explanation: Change flow ratios for other extrusion path types.

settings.name: first_layer_flow_ratio
settings.label: First layer flow ratio
settings.explanation:
This factor affects the amount of material on the first layer for the extrusion path roles listed in this section.

For the first layer, the actual flow ratio for each path role (does not affect brims and skirts) will be multiplied by this value.

settings.name: outer_wall_flow_ratio
settings.label: Outer wall flow ratio
settings.explanation:
This factor affects the amount of material for outer walls.

The actual outer wall flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

settings.name: inner_wall_flow_ratio
settings.label: Inner wall flow ratio
settings.explanation:
This factor affects the amount of material for inner walls.

The actual inner wall flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

settings.name: overhang_flow_ratio
settings.label: Overhang flow ratio
settings.explanation:
This factor affects the amount of material for overhangs.

The actual overhang flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

settings.name: sparse_infill_flow_ratio
settings.label: Sparse infill flow ratio
settings.explanation:
This factor affects the amount of material for sparse infill.

The actual sparse infill flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

settings.name: internal_solid_infill_flow_ratio
settings.label: Internal solid infill flow ratio
settings.explanation:
This factor affects the amount of material for internal solid infill.

The actual internal solid infill flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

settings.name: gap_fill_flow_ratio
settings.label: Gap fill flow ratio
settings.explanation:
This factor affects the amount of material for filling the gaps.

The actual gap filling flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

settings.name: support_flow_ratio
settings.label: Support flow ratio
settings.explanation:
This factor affects the amount of material for support.

The actual support flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

settings.name: support_interface_flow_ratio
settings.label: Support interface flow ratio
settings.explanation:
This factor affects the amount of material for the support interface.

The actual support interface flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

settings.name: only_one_wall_first_layer
settings.label: Only one wall on first layer
settings.explanation: Use only one wall on first layer, to give more space to the bottom infill pattern.

settings.name: only_one_wall_top
settings.label: Only one wall on top surfaces
settings.explanation: Use only one wall on flat top surfaces, to give more space to the top infill pattern.

settings.name: min_width_top_surface
settings.label: One wall threshold
settings.explanation:
If a top surface has to be printed and it's partially covered by another layer, it won't be considered at a top layer where its width is below this value. This can be useful to not let the 'one perimeter on top' trigger on surface that should be covered only by perimeters. This value can be a mm or a % of the perimeter extrusion width.
Warning: If enabled, artifacts can be created if you have some thin features on the next layer, like letters. Set this setting to 0 to remove these artifacts.

settings.name: reduce_crossing_wall
settings.label: Avoid crossing walls
settings.explanation: Detour to avoid traveling across walls, which may cause blobs on the surface.

settings.name: max_travel_detour_distance
settings.label: Avoid crossing walls - Max detour length
settings.explanation: Maximum detour distance for avoiding crossing wall. Don't detour if the detour distance is larger than this value. Detour length could be specified either as an absolute value or as percentage (for example 50%) of a direct travel path. Zero to disable.

settings.name: small_area_infill_flow_compensation
settings.label: Small area flow compensation (beta)
settings.explanation: Enable flow compensation for small infill areas.

settings.name: bridge_flow
settings.label: Bridge flow ratio
settings.explanation:
This value governs the thickness of the external (visible) bridge layer.
Values above 1.0: Increase the amount of material while maintaining line spacing. This can improve line contact and strength.
Values below 1.0: Reduce the amount of material while adjusting line spacing to maintain contact. This can improve sagging.

The actual bridge flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

settings.name: internal_bridge_flow
settings.label: Internal bridge flow ratio
settings.explanation:
This value governs the thickness of the internal bridge layer. This is the first layer over sparse infill so increasing it may increase strength and upper layer quality.
Values above 1.0: Increase the amount of material while maintaining line spacing. This can improve line contact and strength.
Values below 1.0: Reduce the amount of material while adjusting line spacing to maintain contact. This can improve sagging.

The actual bridge flow used is calculated by multiplying this value with the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

settings.name: bridge_density
settings.label: External bridge density
settings.explanation:
Controls the density (spacing) of external bridge lines.
Theoretically, 100% means a solid bridge, but due to the tendency of bridge extrusions to sag, 100% may not be sufficient.

- Higher than 100% density (Recommended Max 125%):
  - Pros: Produces smoother bridge surfaces, as overlapping lines provide additional support during printing.
  - Cons: Can cause overextrusion, which may reduce lower and upper surface quality and increase the risk of warping.

- Lower than 100% density (Min 10%):
  - Pros: Can create a string-like first layer. Faster and with better cooling because there is more space for air to circulate around the extruded bridge.
  - Cons: May lead to sagging and poorer surface finish.

settings.name: internal_bridge_density
settings.label: Internal bridge density
settings.explanation:
Controls the density (spacing) of internal bridge lines.
Internal bridges act as intermediate support between sparse infill and top solid infill and can strongly affect top surface quality.

- Higher than 100% density (Recommended Max 125%):
  - Pros: Improves internal bridge strength and support under top layers, reducing sagging and improving top-surface finish.
  - Cons: Increases material use and print time; excessive density may cause overextrusion and internal stresses.

- Lower than 100% density (Min 10%):
  - Pros: Can reduce pillowing and improve cooling (more airflow through the bridge), and may speed up printing.
  - Cons: May reduce internal support, increasing the risk of sagging and top surface defects.

This option works particularly well when combined with the second internal bridge over infill option to improve bridging further before solid infill is extruded.

settings.name: thick_bridges
settings.label: Thick external bridges
settings.explanation:
If enabled, bridge extrusion uses a line height equal to the nozzle diameter.
This increases bridge strength and reliability, allowing longer spans, but may worsen appearance.
If disabled, bridges may look better but are generally reliable only for shorter spans.

settings.name: thick_internal_bridges
settings.label: Thick internal bridges
settings.explanation:
If enabled, internal bridge extrusion uses a line height equal to the nozzle diameter.
This increases internal bridge strength and reliability when printed over sparse infill, but may worsen appearance.
If disabled, internal bridges may look better but can be less reliable over sparse infill.

settings.name: enable_extra_bridge_layer
settings.label: Extra bridge layers (beta)
settings.explanation:
This option enables the generation of an extra bridge layer over internal and/or external bridges.

Extra bridge layers help improve bridge appearance and reliability, as the solid infill is better supported. This is especially useful in fast printers, where the bridge and solid infill speeds vary greatly. The extra bridge layer results in reduced pillowing on top surfaces, as well as reduced separation of the external bridge layer from its surrounding perimeters.

It is generally recommended to set this to at least 'External bridge only', unless specific issues with the sliced model are found.

Options:
1. Disabled - does not generate second bridge layers. This is the default and is set for compatibility purposes
2. External bridge only - generates second bridge layers for external-facing bridges only. Please note that small bridges that are shorter or narrower than the set number of perimeters will be skipped as they would not benefit from a second bridge layer. If generated, the second bridge layer will be extruded parallel to the first bridge layer to reinforce the bridge strength
3. Internal bridge only - generates second bridge layers for internal bridges over sparse infill only. Please note that the internal bridges count towards the top shell layer count of your model. The second internal bridge layer will be extruded as close to perpendicular to the first as possible. If multiple regions in the same island, with varying bridge angles are present, the last region of that island will be selected as the angle reference
4. Apply to all - generates second bridge layers for both internal and external-facing bridges

settings.name: dont_filter_internal_bridges
settings.label: Filter out small internal bridges
settings.explanation:
This option can help reduce pillowing on top surfaces in heavily slanted or curved models.
By default, small internal bridges are filtered out and the internal solid infill is printed directly over the sparse infill. This works well in most cases, speeding up printing without too much compromise on top surface quality.
However, in heavily slanted or curved models, especially where too low a sparse infill density is used, this may result in curling of the unsupported solid infill, causing pillowing.
Enabling limited filtering or no filtering will print internal bridge layer over slightly unsupported internal solid infill. The options below control the sensitivity of the filtering, i.e. they control where internal bridges are created:
1. Filter - enables this option. This is the default behavior and works well in most cases
2. Limited filtering - creates internal bridges on heavily slanted surfaces while avoiding unnecessary bridges. This works well for most difficult models
3. No filtering - creates internal bridges on every potential internal overhang. This option is useful for heavily slanted top surface models; however, in most cases, it creates too many unnecessary bridges.

settings.name: counterbore_hole_bridging
settings.label: Bridge counterbore holes
settings.explanation:
This option creates bridges for counterbore holes, allowing them to be printed without support. Available modes include:
1. None: No bridge is created
2. Partially Bridged: Only a part of the unsupported area will be bridged
3. Sacrificial Layer: A full sacrificial bridge layer is created

settings.name: detect_overhang_wall
settings.label: Detect overhang walls
settings.explanation: Detect the overhang percentage relative to line width and use different speed to print. For 100%% overhang, bridge speed is used.

settings.name: make_overhang_printable
settings.label: Make overhangs printable
settings.explanation: Modify the geometry to print overhangs without support material.

settings.name: make_overhang_printable_angle
settings.label: Make overhangs printable - Maximum angle
settings.explanation: Maximum angle of overhangs to allow after making more steep overhangs printable.90° will not change the model at all and allow any overhang, while 0 will replace all overhangs with conical material.

settings.name: make_overhang_printable_hole_size
settings.label: Make overhangs printable - Hole area
settings.explanation: Maximum area of a hole in the base of the model before it's filled by conical material. A value of 0 will fill all the holes in the model base.

settings.name: extra_perimeters_on_overhangs
settings.label: Extra perimeters on overhangs
settings.explanation: Create additional perimeter paths over steep overhangs and areas where bridges cannot be anchored.

settings.name: overhang_reverse
settings.label: Reverse on even
settings.explanation:
Extrude perimeters that have a part over an overhang in the reverse direction on even layers. This alternating pattern can drastically improve steep overhangs.

This setting can also help reduce part warping due to the reduction of stresses in the part walls.

settings.name: overhang_reverse_internal_only
settings.label: Reverse only internal perimeters
settings.explanation:
Apply the reverse perimeters logic only on internal perimeters.

This setting greatly reduces part stresses as they are now distributed in alternating directions. This should reduce part warping while also maintaining external wall quality. This feature can be very useful for warp prone material, like ABS/ASA, and also for elastic filaments, like TPU and Silk PLA. It can also help reduce warping on floating regions over supports.

For this setting to be the most effective, it is recommended to set the Reverse Threshold to 0 so that all internal walls print in alternating directions on even layers irrespective of their overhang degree.

settings.name: overhang_reverse_threshold
settings.label: Reverse threshold
settings.explanation:
Number of mm the overhang need to be for the reversal to be considered useful. Can be a % of the perimeter width.
Value 0 enables reversal on every even layers regardless.
When Detect overhang wall is not enabled, this option is ignored and reversal happens on every even layers regardless.

settings.name: wall_loops
settings.label: Wall loops
settings.explanation: Number of walls of every layer.

settings.name: alternate_extra_wall
settings.label: Alternate extra wall
settings.explanation:
This setting adds an extra wall to every other layer. This way the infill gets wedged vertically between the walls, resulting in stronger prints.

When this option is enabled, the ensure vertical shell thickness option needs to be disabled.

Using lightning infill together with this option is not recommended as there is limited infill to anchor the extra perimeters to.

settings.name: detect_thin_wall
settings.label: Detect thin walls
settings.explanation: Detect thin walls which can't contain two line widths, and use single line to print. Maybe not printed very well, because it's not a closed loop.

settings.name: top_shell_layers
settings.label: Top shell layers
settings.explanation: This is the number of solid layers of top shell, including the top surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than top shell thickness, the top shell layers will be increased.

settings.name: top_shell_thickness
settings.label: Top shell thickness
settings.explanation: The number of top solid layers is increased when slicing if the thickness calculated by top shell layers is thinner than this value. This can avoid having too thin shell when layer height is small. 0 means that this setting is disabled and thickness of top shell is absolutely determined by top shell layers.

settings.name: top_surface_density
settings.label: Top surface density
settings.explanation: Density of top surface layer. A value of 100% creates a fully solid, smooth top layer. Reducing this value results in a textured top surface, according to the chosen top surface pattern. A value of 0% will result in only the walls on the top layer being created. Intended for aesthetic or functional purposes, not to fix issues such as over-extrusion.

settings.name: top_surface_pattern
settings.label: Top surface pattern
settings.explanation: Line pattern of top surface infill.

settings.name: bottom_shell_layers
settings.label: Bottom shell layers
settings.explanation: This is the number of solid layers of bottom shell, including the bottom surface layer. When the thickness calculated by this value is thinner than bottom shell thickness, the bottom shell layers will be increased.

settings.name: bottom_shell_thickness
settings.label: Bottom shell thickness
settings.explanation: The number of bottom solid layers is increased when slicing if the thickness calculated by bottom shell layers is thinner than this value. This can avoid having too thin shell when layer height is small. 0 means that this setting is disabled and thickness of bottom shell is absolutely determined by bottom shell layers.

settings.name: bottom_surface_density
settings.label: Bottom surface density
settings.explanation:
Density of the bottom surface layer. Intended for aesthetic or functional purposes, not to fix issues such as over-extrusion.
WARNING: Lowering this value may negatively affect bed adhesion.

settings.name: bottom_surface_pattern
settings.label: Bottom surface pattern
settings.explanation: Line pattern of bottom surface infill, not bridge infill.

settings.name: top_bottom_infill_wall_overlap
settings.label: Top/Bottom solid infill/wall overlap
settings.explanation: Top solid infill area is enlarged slightly to overlap with wall for better bonding and to minimize the appearance of pinholes where the top infill meets the walls. A value of 25-30% is a good starting point, minimizing the appearance of pinholes. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill.

settings.name: sparse_infill_density
settings.label: Sparse infill density
settings.explanation: Density of internal sparse infill, 100% turns all sparse infill into solid infill and internal solid infill pattern will be used.

settings.name: fill_multiline
settings.label: Fill Multiline
settings.explanation: Using multiple lines for the infill pattern, if supported by infill pattern.

settings.name: sparse_infill_pattern
settings.label: Sparse infill pattern
settings.explanation: Line pattern for internal sparse infill.

settings.name: gyroid_optimized
settings.label: Z-buckling bias optimization (experimental)
settings.explanation: Tightens the gyroid wave along the Z (vertical) axis at low infill density to shorten the effective vertical column length and improve Z-axis compression buckling resistance. Filament use is preserved. No effect at ~30% sparse infill density and above. Only applies when Sparse infill pattern is set to Gyroid.

settings.name: infill_direction
settings.label: Sparse infill direction
settings.explanation: Angle for sparse infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of line.

settings.name: sparse_infill_rotate_template
settings.label: Sparse infill rotation template
settings.explanation: Rotate the sparse infill direction per layer using a template of angles. Enter comma-separated degrees (e.g., '0,30,60,90'). Angles are applied in order by layer and repeat when the list ends. Advanced syntax is supported: '+5' rotates +5° every layer; '+5#5' rotates +5° every 5 layers. See the Wiki for details. When a template is set, the standard infill direction setting is ignored. Note: some infill patterns (e.g., Gyroid) control rotation themselves; use with care.

settings.name: skin_infill_density
settings.label: Skin infill density
settings.explanation: The portion of the model's outer surface within a certain depth range is called the skin. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section. When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skin densities, this area will not be split into two separate regions. Default is as same as infill density.

settings.name: skeleton_infill_density
settings.label: Skeleton infill density
settings.explanation: The remaining part of the model contour after removing a certain depth from the surface is called the skeleton. This parameter is used to adjust the density of this section. When two regions have the same sparse infill settings but different skeleton densities, their skeleton areas will develop overlapping sections. Default is as same as infill density.

settings.name: infill_lock_depth
settings.label: Infill lock depth
settings.explanation: The parameter sets the overlapping depth between the interior and skin.

settings.name: skin_infill_depth
settings.label: Skin infill depth
settings.explanation: The parameter sets the depth of skin.

settings.name: skin_infill_line_width
settings.label: Skin line width
settings.explanation: Adjust the line width of the selected skin paths.

settings.name: skeleton_infill_line_width
settings.label: Skeleton line width
settings.explanation: Adjust the line width of the selected skeleton paths.

settings.name: symmetric_infill_y_axis
settings.label: Symmetric infill Y axis
settings.explanation: If the model has two parts that are symmetric about the Y axis, and you want these parts to have symmetric textures, please click this option on one of the parts.

settings.name: infill_shift_step
settings.label: Infill shift step
settings.explanation: This parameter adds a slight displacement to each layer of infill to create a cross texture.

settings.name: lateral_lattice_angle_1
settings.label: Lateral lattice angle 1
settings.explanation: The angle of the first set of Lateral lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

settings.name: lateral_lattice_angle_2
settings.label: Lateral lattice angle 2
settings.explanation: The angle of the second set of Lateral lattice elements in the Z direction. Zero is vertical.

settings.name: infill_overhang_angle
settings.label: Infill overhang angle
settings.explanation: The angle of the infill angled lines. 60° will result in a pure honeycomb.

settings.name: lightning_overhang_angle
settings.label: Lightning overhang angle
settings.explanation: Maximum overhang angle for Lightning infill support propagation.

settings.name: lightning_prune_angle
settings.label: Prune angle
settings.explanation:
Controls how aggressively short or unsupported Lightning branches are pruned.
This angle is converted internally to a per-layer distance.

settings.name: lightning_straightening_angle
settings.label: Straightening angle
settings.explanation: Maximum straightening angle used to simplify Lightning branches.

settings.name: infill_anchor_max
settings.label: Maximum length of the infill anchor
settings.explanation:
Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Orca Slicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than this parameter is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to infill_anchor, but no longer than this parameter.
If set to 0, the old algorithm for infill connection will be used, it should create the same result as with 1000 & 0.

settings.name: infill_anchor
settings.label: Sparse infill anchor length
settings.explanation:
Connect an infill line to an internal perimeter with a short segment of an additional perimeter. If expressed as percentage (example: 15%) it is calculated over infill extrusion width. Orca Slicer tries to connect two close infill lines to a short perimeter segment. If no such perimeter segment shorter than infill_anchor_max is found, the infill line is connected to a perimeter segment at just one side and the length of the perimeter segment taken is limited to this parameter, but no longer than anchor_length_max.
Set this parameter to zero to disable anchoring perimeters connected to a single infill line.

settings.name: internal_solid_infill_pattern
settings.label: Internal solid infill pattern
settings.explanation: Line pattern of internal solid infill. if the detect narrow internal solid infill be enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the small area.

settings.name: solid_infill_direction
settings.label: Solid infill direction
settings.explanation: Angle for solid infill pattern, which controls the start or main direction of line.

settings.name: solid_infill_rotate_template
settings.label: Solid infill rotation template
settings.explanation: This parameter adds a rotation of solid infill direction to each layer according to the specified template. The template is a comma-separated list of angles in degrees, e.g. '0,90'. The first angle is applied to the first layer, the second angle to the second layer, and so on. If there are more layers than angles, the angles will be repeated. Note that not all solid infill patterns support rotation.

settings.name: gap_fill_target
settings.label: Apply gap fill
settings.explanation:
Enables gap fill for the selected solid surfaces. The minimum gap length that will be filled can be controlled from the filter out tiny gaps option below.

Options:
1. Everywhere: Applies gap fill to top, bottom and internal solid surfaces for maximum strength
2. Top and Bottom surfaces: Applies gap fill to top and bottom surfaces only, balancing print speed, reducing potential over extrusion in the solid infill and making sure the top and bottom surfaces have no pinhole gaps
3. Nowhere: Disables gap fill for all solid infill areas

Note that if using the classic perimeter generator, gap fill may also be generated between perimeters, if a full width line cannot fit between them. That perimeter gap fill is not controlled by this setting.

If you would like all gap fill, including the classic perimeter generated one, removed, set the filter out tiny gaps value to a large number, like 999999.

However this is not advised, as gap fill between perimeters is contributing to the model's strength. For models where excessive gap fill is generated between perimeters, a better option would be to switch to the arachne wall generator and use this option to control whether the cosmetic top and bottom surface gap fill is generated.

settings.name: filter_out_gap_fill
settings.label: Filter out tiny gaps
settings.explanation: Don't print gap fill with a length is smaller than the threshold specified (in mm). This setting applies to top, bottom and solid infill and, if using the classic perimeter generator, to wall gap fill.

settings.name: infill_wall_overlap
settings.label: Infill/Wall overlap
settings.explanation: Infill area is enlarged slightly to overlap with wall for better bonding. The percentage value is relative to line width of sparse infill. Set this value to ~10-15% to minimize potential over extrusion and accumulation of material resulting in rough top surfaces.

settings.name: align_infill_direction_to_model
settings.label: Align infill direction to model
settings.explanation:
Aligns infill, bridge, ironing and surface fill directions to follow the model's orientation on the build plate.
When enabled, directions rotate with the model to maintain optimal strength characteristics.

settings.name: extra_solid_infills
settings.label: Insert solid layers
settings.explanation: Insert solid infill at specific layers. Use N to insert every Nth layer, N#K to insert K consecutive solid layers every N layers (K is optional, e.g. '5#' equals '5#1'), or a comma-separated list (e.g. 1,7,9) to insert at explicit layers. Layers are 1-based.

settings.name: bridge_angle
settings.label: External bridge infill direction
settings.explanation:
External Bridging angle override.
If left to zero, the bridging angle will be calculated automatically for each specific bridge.
Otherwise the provided angle will be used according to:
 - The absolute coordinates
 - The absolute coordinates + Model rotation: If Align infill direction to model is enabled
 - The optimal automatic angle + this value: If 'Relative Bridge Angle' is enabled

Use 180° for zero absolute angle.

settings.name: internal_bridge_angle
settings.label: Internal bridge infill direction
settings.explanation:
Internal Bridging angle override.
If left to zero, the bridging angle will be calculated automatically for each specific bridge.
Otherwise the provided angle will be used according to:
 - The absolute coordinates
 - The absolute coordinates + Model rotation: If Align infill direction to model is enabled
 - The optimal automatic angle + this value: If 'Relative Bridge Angle' is enabled

Use 180° for zero absolute angle.

settings.name: relative_bridge_angle
settings.label: Relative bridge angle
settings.explanation: When enabled, the bridge angle values are added to the automatically calculated bridge direction instead of overriding it.

settings.name: minimum_sparse_infill_area
settings.label: Minimum sparse infill threshold
settings.explanation: Sparse infill areas smaller than this threshold value are replaced by internal solid infill.

settings.name: infill_combination
settings.label: Infill combination
settings.explanation: Automatically Combine sparse infill of several layers to print together to reduce time. Wall is still printed with original layer height.

settings.name: infill_combination_max_layer_height
settings.label: Infill combination - Max layer height
settings.explanation:
Maximum layer height for the combined sparse infill.

Set it to 0 or 100% to use the nozzle diameter (for maximum reduction in print time) or a value of ~80% to maximize sparse infill strength.

The number of layers over which infill is combined is derived by dividing this value with the layer height and rounded down to the nearest decimal.

Use either absolute mm values (eg. 0.32mm for a 0.4mm nozzle) or % values (eg 80%). This value must not be larger than the nozzle diameter.

settings.name: detect_narrow_internal_solid_infill
settings.label: Detect narrow internal solid infills
settings.explanation: This option will auto-detect narrow internal solid infill areas. If enabled, the concentric pattern will be used for the area to speed up printing. Otherwise, the rectilinear pattern will be used by default.

settings.name: ensure_vertical_shell_thickness
settings.label: Ensure vertical shell thickness
settings.explanation:
Add solid infill near sloping surfaces to guarantee the vertical shell thickness (top+bottom solid layers)
None: No solid infill will be added anywhere. Caution: Use this option carefully if your model has sloped surfaces
Critical Only: Avoid adding solid infill for walls
Moderate: Add solid infill for heavily sloping surfaces only
All: Add solid infill for all suitable sloping surfaces
Default value is All.

settings.name: initial_layer_speed
settings.label: First layer
settings.explanation: Speed of the first layer except the solid infill part.

settings.name: initial_layer_infill_speed
settings.label: First layer infill
settings.explanation: Speed of solid infill part of the first layer.

settings.name: initial_layer_travel_speed
settings.label: First layer travel speed
settings.explanation: Travel speed of the first layer.

settings.name: slow_down_layers
settings.label: Number of slow layers
settings.explanation: The first few layers are printed slower than normal. The speed is gradually increased in a linear fashion over the specified number of layers.

settings.name: outer_wall_speed
settings.label: Outer wall
settings.explanation: Speed of outer wall which is outermost and visible. It's used to be slower than inner wall speed to get better quality.

settings.name: inner_wall_speed
settings.label: Inner wall
settings.explanation: Speed of inner wall.

settings.name: small_perimeter_speed
settings.label: Small perimeters
settings.explanation: This separate setting will affect the speed of perimeters having radius <= small_perimeter_threshold (usually holes). If expressed as percentage (for example: 80%) it will be calculated on the outer wall speed setting above. Set to zero for auto.

settings.name: small_perimeter_threshold
settings.label: Small perimeters threshold
settings.explanation: This sets the threshold for small perimeter length. Default threshold is 0mm.

settings.name: sparse_infill_speed
settings.label: Sparse infill
settings.explanation: Speed of internal sparse infill.

settings.name: internal_solid_infill_speed
settings.label: Internal solid infill
settings.explanation: Speed of internal solid infill, not the top and bottom surface.

settings.name: top_surface_speed
settings.label: Top surface
settings.explanation: Speed of top surface infill which is solid.

settings.name: gap_infill_speed
settings.label: Gap infill
settings.explanation: Speed of gap infill. Gap usually has irregular line width and should be printed more slowly.

settings.name: ironing_speed
settings.label: Ironing speed
settings.explanation: Print speed of ironing lines.

settings.name: support_speed
settings.label: Support
settings.explanation: Speed of support.

settings.name: support_interface_speed
settings.label: Support interface
settings.explanation: Speed of support interface.

settings.name: enable_overhang_speed
settings.label: Slow down for overhang
settings.explanation: Enable this option to slow printing down for different overhang degree.

settings.name: slowdown_for_curled_perimeters
settings.label: Slow down for curled perimeters
settings.explanation:
Enable this option to slow down printing in areas where perimeters may have curled upwards.
For example, additional slowdown will be applied when printing overhangs on sharp corners like the front of the Benchy hull, reducing curling which compounds over multiple layers.

It is generally recommended to have this option switched on unless your printer cooling is powerful enough or the print speed is slow enough that perimeter curling does not happen. 
If printing with a high external perimeter speed, this parameter may introduce wall artifacts when slowing down, due to the potentially large variance in print speeds causing the extruder to be unable to keep up with the requested flow change.
Root cause of these artifacts is most likely PA tuning being slightly off, especially when combined with a high PA smooth time.

Recommendations when enabling this option:
1. Reduce Pressure Advance smooth time to 0.015 - 0.02 so the extruder reacts quickly to the speed changes.
2. Increase the minimum print speeds to limit the magnitude of the slowdown and reduce the variance between fast and slow segments.
3. If artifacts still appear, enable Extrusion Rate Smoothing (ERS) to further smooth the flow transitions.

Note: When this option is enabled, overhang perimeters are treated like overhangs, meaning the overhang speed is applied even if the overhanging perimeter is part of a bridge.
For example, when the perimeters are 100% overhanging, with no wall supporting them from underneath, the 100% overhang speed will be applied.

settings.name: bridge_speed
settings.label: External
settings.explanation:
Speed of the externally visible bridge extrusions.

In addition, if Slow down for curled perimeters is disabled or Classic overhang mode is enabled, it will be the print speed of overhang walls that are supported by less than 13%, whether they are part of a bridge or an overhang.

settings.name: internal_bridge_speed
settings.label: Internal
settings.explanation: Speed of internal bridges. If the value is expressed as a percentage, it will be calculated based on the bridge_speed. Default value is 150%.

settings.name: travel_speed
settings.label: Travel
settings.explanation: Speed of travel which is faster and without extrusion.

settings.name: default_acceleration
settings.label: Normal printing
settings.explanation: The default acceleration of both normal printing and travel except initial layer.

settings.name: outer_wall_acceleration
settings.label: Outer wall
settings.explanation: Acceleration of outer wall. Using a lower value can improve quality.

settings.name: inner_wall_acceleration
settings.label: Inner wall
settings.explanation: Acceleration of inner walls.

settings.name: bridge_acceleration
settings.label: Bridge
settings.explanation: Acceleration of bridges. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 50%), it will be calculated based on the outer wall acceleration.

settings.name: sparse_infill_acceleration
settings.label: Sparse infill
settings.explanation: Acceleration of sparse infill. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 100%), it will be calculated based on the default acceleration.

settings.name: internal_solid_infill_acceleration
settings.label: Internal solid infill
settings.explanation: Acceleration of internal solid infill. If the value is expressed as a percentage (e.g. 100%), it will be calculated based on the default acceleration.

settings.name: initial_layer_acceleration
settings.label: First layer
settings.explanation: Acceleration of the first layer. Using a lower value can improve build plate adhesion.

settings.name: initial_layer_travel_acceleration
settings.label: First layer travel
settings.explanation:
Travel acceleration of first layer.
The percentage value is relative to Travel Acceleration.

settings.name: top_surface_acceleration
settings.label: Top surface
settings.explanation: Acceleration of top surface infill. Using a lower value may improve top surface quality.

settings.name: travel_acceleration
settings.label: Travel
settings.explanation: Acceleration of travel moves.

settings.name: accel_to_decel_enable
settings.label: Enable accel_to_decel
settings.explanation: Klipper's max_accel_to_decel will be adjusted automatically.

settings.name: accel_to_decel_factor
settings.label: accel_to_decel
settings.explanation: Klipper's max_accel_to_decel will be adjusted to this %% of acceleration.

settings.name: default_junction_deviation
settings.label: Junction Deviation
settings.explanation: Marlin Firmware Junction Deviation (replaces the traditional XY Jerk setting).

settings.name: default_jerk
settings.label: Default
settings.explanation: Default jerk.

settings.name: outer_wall_jerk
settings.label: Outer wall
settings.explanation: Jerk of outer walls.

settings.name: inner_wall_jerk
settings.label: Inner wall
settings.explanation: Jerk of inner walls.

settings.name: infill_jerk
settings.label: Infill
settings.explanation: Jerk for infill.

settings.name: top_surface_jerk
settings.label: Top surface
settings.explanation: Jerk for top surface.

settings.name: initial_layer_jerk
settings.label: First layer
settings.explanation: Jerk for the first layer.

settings.name: initial_layer_travel_jerk
settings.label: First layer travel
settings.explanation:
Travel jerk of first layer.
The percentage value is relative to Travel Jerk.

settings.name: travel_jerk
settings.label: Travel
settings.explanation: Jerk for travel.

settings.name: max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope
settings.label: Extrusion rate smoothing
settings.explanation:
This parameter smooths out sudden extrusion rate changes that happen when the printer transitions from printing a high flow (high speed/larger width) extrusion to a lower flow (lower speed/smaller width) extrusion and vice versa.

It defines the maximum rate by which the extruded volumetric flow in mm³/s can change over time. Higher values mean higher extrusion rate changes are allowed, resulting in faster speed transitions.

A value of 0 disables the feature.

For a high speed, high flow direct drive printer (like the Bambu lab or Voron) this value is usually not needed. However it can provide some marginal benefit in certain cases where feature speeds vary greatly. For example, when there are aggressive slowdowns due to overhangs. In these cases a high value of around 300-350 mm³/s² is recommended as this allows for just enough smoothing to assist pressure advance achieve a smoother flow transition.

For slower printers without pressure advance, the value should be set much lower. A value of 10-15 mm³/s² is a good starting point for direct drive extruders and 5-10 mm³/s² for Bowden style.

This feature is known as Pressure Equalizer in Prusa slicer.

Note: this parameter disables arc fitting.

settings.name: max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_segment_length
settings.label: Smoothing segment length
settings.explanation:
A lower value results in smoother extrusion rate transitions. However, this results in a significantly larger G-code file and more instructions for the printer to process.

Default value of 3 works well for most cases. If your printer is stuttering, increase this value to reduce the number of adjustments made.

Allowed values: 0.5-5

settings.name: extrusion_rate_smoothing_external_perimeter_only
settings.label: Apply only on external features
settings.explanation: Applies extrusion rate smoothing only on external perimeters and overhangs. This can help reduce artefacts due to sharp speed transitions on externally visible overhangs without impacting the print speed of features that will not be visible to the user.

settings.name: enable_support
settings.label: Enable support
settings.explanation: Enable support generation.

settings.name: support_type
settings.label: Type
settings.explanation: Normal (auto) and Tree (auto) are used to generate support automatically. If Normal (manual) or Tree (manual) is selected, only support enforcers are generated.

settings.name: support_style
settings.label: Style
settings.explanation:
Style and shape of the support. For normal support, projecting the supports into a regular grid will create more stable supports (default), while snug support towers will save material and reduce object scarring.
For tree support, slim and organic style will merge branches more aggressively and save a lot of material (default organic), while hybrid style will create similar structure to normal support under large flat overhangs.

settings.name: support_threshold_angle
settings.label: Threshold angle
settings.explanation:
Support will be generated for overhangs whose slope angle is below the threshold. The smaller this value is, the steeper the overhang that can be printed without support.
Note: If set to 0, normal supports use the Threshold overlap instead, while tree supports fall back to a default value of 30.

settings.name: support_threshold_overlap
settings.label: Threshold overlap
settings.explanation: If threshold angle is zero, support will be generated for overhangs whose overlap is below the threshold. The smaller this value is, the steeper the overhang that can be printed without support.

settings.name: raft_first_layer_density
settings.label: First layer density
settings.explanation: Density of the first raft or support layer.

settings.name: raft_first_layer_expansion
settings.label: First layer expansion
settings.explanation: Expand the first raft or support layer to improve bed plate adhesion.

settings.name: support_on_build_plate_only
settings.label: On build plate only
settings.explanation: Don't create support on model surface, only on build plate.

settings.name: support_critical_regions_only
settings.label: Support critical regions only
settings.explanation: Only create support for critical regions including sharp tail, cantilever, etc.

settings.name: support_remove_small_overhang
settings.label: Ignore small overhangs
settings.explanation: Ignore small overhangs that possibly don't require support.

settings.name: raft_layers
settings.label: Raft layers
settings.explanation: Object will be raised by this number of support layers. Use this function to avoid warping when printing ABS.

settings.name: raft_contact_distance
settings.label: Raft contact Z distance
settings.explanation: Z gap between raft and object. If Support Top Z Distance is 0, this value is ignored and the object is printed in direct contact with the raft (no gap).

settings.name: support_filament
settings.label: Support/raft base
settings.explanation:
Filament to print support base and raft.
"Default" means no specific filament for support and current filament is used.

settings.name: support_interface_filament
settings.label: Support/raft interface
settings.explanation:
Filament to print support interface.
"Default" means no specific filament for support interface and current filament is used.

settings.name: support_interface_not_for_body
settings.label: Avoid interface filament for base
settings.explanation: Avoid using support interface filament to print support base if possible.

settings.name: support_ironing
settings.label: Ironing Support Interface
settings.explanation: Ironing is using small flow to print on same height of support interface again to make it more smooth. This setting controls whether support interface being ironed. When enabled, support interface will be extruded as solid too.

settings.name: support_ironing_pattern
settings.label: Support Ironing Pattern
settings.explanation: The pattern that will be used when ironing.

settings.name: support_ironing_flow
settings.label: Support Ironing flow
settings.explanation: The amount of material to extrude during ironing. Relative to flow of normal support interface layer height. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface.

settings.name: support_ironing_spacing
settings.label: Support Ironing line spacing
settings.explanation: The distance between the lines of ironing.

settings.name: support_top_z_distance
settings.label: Top Z distance
settings.explanation: Z gap between the support's top and object.

settings.name: support_bottom_z_distance
settings.label: Bottom Z distance
settings.explanation: Z gap between the object and the support bottom. If Support Top Z Distance is 0 and the bottom has interface layers, this value is ignored and the support is printed in direct contact with the object (no gap).

settings.name: tree_support_wall_count
settings.label: Support wall loops
settings.explanation: This setting specifies the count of support walls in the range of [0,2]. 0 means auto.

settings.name: support_base_pattern
settings.label: Base pattern
settings.explanation:
Line pattern of support.

The Default option for Tree supports is Hollow, which means no base pattern. For other support types, the Default option is the Rectilinear pattern.

NOTE: For Organic supports, the two walls are supported only with the Hollow/Default base pattern. The Lightning base pattern is supported only by Tree Slim/Strong/Hybrid supports. For the other support types, the Rectilinear will be used instead of Lightning.

settings.name: support_base_pattern_spacing
settings.label: Base pattern spacing
settings.explanation: Spacing between support lines.

settings.name: support_angle
settings.label: Pattern angle
settings.explanation: Use this setting to rotate the support pattern on the horizontal plane.

settings.name: support_interface_top_layers
settings.label: Top interface layers
settings.explanation: Number of top interface layers.

settings.name: support_interface_bottom_layers
settings.label: Bottom interface layers
settings.explanation: Number of bottom interface layers.

settings.name: support_interface_pattern
settings.label: Interface pattern
settings.explanation: Line pattern of support interface. Default pattern for non-soluble support interface is Rectilinear, while default pattern for soluble support interface is Concentric.

settings.name: support_interface_spacing
settings.label: Top interface spacing
settings.explanation:
Spacing of interface lines. Zero means solid interface.
Force using solid interface when support ironing is enabled.

settings.name: support_bottom_interface_spacing
settings.label: Bottom interface spacing
settings.explanation: Spacing of bottom interface lines. Zero means solid interface.

settings.name: support_expansion
settings.label: Normal Support expansion
settings.explanation: Expand (+) or shrink (-) the horizontal span of normal support.

settings.name: support_object_xy_distance
settings.label: Support/object XY distance
settings.explanation: XY separation between an object and its support.

settings.name: support_object_first_layer_gap
settings.label: Support/object first layer gap
settings.explanation: XY separation between an object and its support at the first layer.

settings.name: bridge_no_support
settings.label: Don't support bridges
settings.explanation: Don't support the whole bridge area which make support very large. Bridges can usually be printed directly without support if not very long.

settings.name: max_bridge_length
settings.label: Max bridge length
settings.explanation: Max length of bridges that don't need support. Set it to 0 if you want all bridges to be supported, and set it to a very large value if you don't want any bridges to be supported.

settings.name: independent_support_layer_height
settings.label: Independent support layer height
settings.explanation: Support layer uses layer height independent with object layer. This is to support customizing Z-gap and save print time. This option will be invalid when the prime tower is enabled.

settings.name: tree_support_tip_diameter
settings.label: Tip Diameter
settings.explanation: Branch tip diameter for organic supports.

settings.name: tree_support_branch_distance
settings.label: Tree support branch distance
settings.explanation: This setting determines the distance between neighboring tree support nodes.

settings.name: tree_support_branch_distance_organic
settings.label: Tree support branch distance
settings.explanation: This setting determines the distance between neighboring tree support nodes.

settings.name: tree_support_top_rate
settings.label: Branch Density
settings.explanation: Adjusts the density of the support structure used to generate the tips of the branches. A higher value results in better overhangs but the supports are harder to remove, thus it is recommended to enable top support interfaces instead of a high branch density value if dense interfaces are needed.

settings.name: tree_support_branch_diameter
settings.label: Tree support branch diameter
settings.explanation: This setting determines the initial diameter of support nodes.

settings.name: tree_support_branch_diameter_organic
settings.label: Tree support branch diameter
settings.explanation: This setting determines the initial diameter of support nodes.

settings.name: tree_support_branch_diameter_angle
settings.label: Branch Diameter Angle
settings.explanation: The angle of the branches' diameter as they gradually become thicker towards the bottom. An angle of 0 will cause the branches to have uniform thickness over their length. A bit of an angle can increase stability of the organic support.

settings.name: tree_support_branch_angle
settings.label: Tree support branch angle
settings.explanation: This setting determines the maximum overhang angle that the branches of tree support are allowed to make. If the angle is increased, the branches can be printed more horizontally, allowing them to reach farther.

settings.name: tree_support_branch_angle_organic
settings.label: Tree support branch angle
settings.explanation: This setting determines the maximum overhang angle that the branches of tree support are allowed to make. If the angle is increased, the branches can be printed more horizontally, allowing them to reach farther.

settings.name: tree_support_angle_slow
settings.label: Preferred Branch Angle
settings.explanation: The preferred angle of the branches, when they do not have to avoid the model. Use a lower angle to make them more vertical and more stable. Use a higher angle for branches to merge faster.

settings.name: tree_support_auto_brim
settings.label: Auto brim width
settings.explanation: Enabling this option means the width of the brim for tree support will be automatically calculated.

settings.name: tree_support_brim_width
settings.label: Tree support brim width
settings.explanation: Distance from tree branch to the outermost brim line.

settings.name: enable_prime_tower
settings.label: Enable
settings.explanation: The wiping tower can be used to clean up the residue on the nozzle and stabilize the chamber pressure inside the nozzle, in order to avoid appearance defects when printing objects.

settings.name: prime_tower_skip_points
settings.label: Skip points
settings.explanation: The wall of prime tower will skip the start points of wipe path.

settings.name: enable_tower_interface_features
settings.label: Enable tower interface features
settings.explanation: Enable optimized prime tower interface behavior when different materials meet.

settings.name: enable_tower_interface_cooldown_during_tower
settings.label: Cool down from interface boost during prime tower
settings.explanation: When interface-layer temperature boost is active, set the nozzle back to print temperature at the start of the prime tower so it cools down during the tower.

settings.name: prime_tower_enable_framework
settings.label: Internal ribs
settings.explanation: Enable internal ribs to increase the stability of the prime tower.

settings.name: prime_tower_width
settings.label: Width
settings.explanation: Width of the prime tower.

settings.name: prime_volume
settings.label: Prime volume
settings.explanation: The volume of material to prime extruder on tower.

settings.name: prime_tower_brim_width
settings.label: Brim width
settings.explanation: Brim width of prime tower, negative number means auto calculated width based on the height of prime tower.

settings.name: prime_tower_infill_gap
settings.label: Infill gap
settings.explanation: Infill gap.

settings.name: wipe_tower_rotation_angle
settings.label: Wipe tower rotation angle
settings.explanation: Wipe tower rotation angle with respect to X axis.

settings.name: wipe_tower_bridging
settings.label: Maximal bridging distance
settings.explanation: Maximal distance between supports on sparse infill sections.

settings.name: wipe_tower_extra_spacing
settings.label: Wipe tower purge lines spacing
settings.explanation: Spacing of purge lines on the wipe tower.

settings.name: wipe_tower_extra_flow
settings.label: Extra flow for purging
settings.explanation: Extra flow used for the purging lines on the wipe tower. This makes the purging lines thicker or narrower than they normally would be. The spacing is adjusted automatically.

settings.name: wipe_tower_max_purge_speed
settings.label: Maximum wipe tower print speed
settings.explanation:
The maximum print speed when purging in the wipe tower and printing the wipe tower sparse layers. When purging, if the sparse infill speed or calculated speed from the filament max volumetric speed is lower, the lowest will be used instead.

When printing the sparse layers, if the internal perimeter speed or calculated speed from the filament max volumetric speed is lower, the lowest will be used instead.

Increasing this speed may affect the tower's stability as well as increase the force with which the nozzle collides with any blobs that may have formed on the wipe tower.

Before increasing this parameter beyond the default of 90 mm/s, make sure your printer can reliably bridge at the increased speeds and that ooze when tool changing is well controlled.

For the wipe tower external perimeters the internal perimeter speed is used regardless of this setting.

settings.name: wipe_tower_wall_type
settings.label: Wall type
settings.explanation:
Wipe tower outer wall type.
1. Rectangle: The default wall type, a rectangle with fixed width and height.
2. Cone: A cone with a fillet at the bottom to help stabilize the wipe tower.
3. Rib: Adds four ribs to the tower wall for enhanced stability.

settings.name: wipe_tower_cone_angle
settings.label: Stabilization cone apex angle
settings.explanation: Angle at the apex of the cone that is used to stabilize the wipe tower. Larger angle means wider base.

settings.name: wipe_tower_extra_rib_length
settings.label: Extra rib length
settings.explanation: Positive values can increase the size of the rib wall, while negative values can reduce the size. However, the size of the rib wall can not be smaller than that determined by the cleaning volume.

settings.name: wipe_tower_rib_width
settings.label: Rib width
settings.explanation: Rib width is always less than half the prime tower side length.

settings.name: wipe_tower_fillet_wall
settings.label: Fillet wall
settings.explanation: The wall of prime tower will fillet.

settings.name: wipe_tower_no_sparse_layers
settings.label: No sparse layers (beta)
settings.explanation: If enabled, the wipe tower will not be printed on layers with no tool changes. On layers with a tool change, extruder will travel downward to print the wipe tower. User is responsible for ensuring there is no collision with the print.

settings.name: single_extruder_multi_material_priming
settings.label: Prime all printing extruders
settings.explanation: If enabled, all printing extruders will be primed at the front edge of the print bed at the start of the print.

settings.name: outer_wall_filament_id
settings.label: Outer walls
settings.explanation:
Filament to print outer walls.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

settings.name: inner_wall_filament_id
settings.label: Inner walls
settings.explanation:
Filament to print inner walls.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

settings.name: sparse_infill_filament_id
settings.label: Infill
settings.explanation:
Filament to print internal sparse infill.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

settings.name: internal_solid_filament_id
settings.label: Internal solid infill
settings.explanation:
Filament to print internal solid infill.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

settings.name: top_surface_filament_id
settings.label: Top surface
settings.explanation:
Filament to print top surface.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

settings.name: bottom_surface_filament_id
settings.label: Bottom surface
settings.explanation:
Filament to print bottom surface.
"Default" uses the active object/part filament.

settings.name: wipe_tower_filament
settings.label: Wipe tower
settings.explanation: The extruder to use when printing perimeter of the wipe tower. Set to 0 to use the one that is available (non-soluble would be preferred).

settings.name: ooze_prevention
settings.label: Enable
settings.explanation: This option will drop the temperature of the inactive extruders to prevent oozing.

settings.name: standby_temperature_delta
settings.label: Temperature variation
