settings.explanation: Temperature difference to be applied when an extruder is not active. The value is not used when 'idle_temperature' in filament settings is set to non-zero value.

settings.name: preheat_time
settings.label: Preheat time
settings.explanation: To reduce the waiting time after tool change, Orca can preheat the next tool while the current tool is still in use. This setting specifies the time in seconds to preheat the next tool. Orca will insert a M104 command to preheat the tool in advance.

settings.name: preheat_steps
settings.label: Preheat steps
settings.explanation: Insert multiple preheat commands (e.g. M104.1). Only useful for Prusa XL. For other printers, please set it to 1.

settings.name: flush_into_infill
settings.label: Flush into objects' infill
settings.explanation: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' infills. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. If the walls are printed with transparent filament, the mixed color infill will be seen outside. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.

settings.name: flush_into_objects
settings.label: Flush into this object
settings.explanation: This object will be used to purge the nozzle after a filament change to save filament and decrease the print time. Colors of the objects will be mixed as a result. It will not take effect unless the prime tower is enabled.

settings.name: flush_into_support
settings.label: Flush into objects' support
settings.explanation: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' support. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. It will not take effect, unless the prime tower is enabled.

settings.name: interlocking_beam
settings.label: Use beam interlocking
settings.explanation: Generate interlocking beam structure at the locations where different filaments touch. This improves the adhesion between filaments, especially models printed in different materials.

settings.name: interface_shells
settings.label: Interface shells
settings.explanation: Force the generation of solid shells between adjacent materials/volumes. Useful for multi-extruder prints with translucent materials or manual soluble support material.

settings.name: mmu_segmented_region_max_width
settings.label: Maximum width of a segmented region
settings.explanation: Maximum width of a segmented region. Zero disables this feature.

settings.name: mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth
settings.label: Interlocking depth of a segmented region
settings.explanation: Interlocking depth of a segmented region. It will be ignored if "mmu_segmented_region_max_width" is zero or if "mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth" is bigger than "mmu_segmented_region_max_width". Zero disables this feature.

settings.name: interlocking_beam_width
settings.label: Interlocking beam width
settings.explanation: The width of the interlocking structure beams.

settings.name: interlocking_orientation
settings.label: Interlocking direction
settings.explanation: Orientation of interlock beams.

settings.name: interlocking_beam_layer_count
settings.label: Interlocking beam layers
settings.explanation: The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.

settings.name: interlocking_depth
settings.label: Interlocking depth
settings.explanation: The distance from the boundary between filaments to generate interlocking structure, measured in cells. Too few cells will result in poor adhesion.

settings.name: interlocking_boundary_avoidance
settings.label: Interlocking boundary avoidance
settings.explanation: The distance from the outside of a model where interlocking structures will not be generated, measured in cells.

settings.name: skirt_loops
settings.label: Skirt loops
settings.explanation: Number of loops for the skirt. Zero means disabling skirt.

settings.name: skirt_type
settings.label: Skirt type
settings.explanation: Combined - single skirt for all objects, Per object - individual object skirt.

settings.name: min_skirt_length
settings.label: Skirt minimum extrusion length
settings.explanation:
Minimum filament extrusion length in mm when printing the skirt. Zero means this feature is disabled.

Using a non-zero value is useful if the printer is set up to print without a prime line.
Final number of loops is not taking into account while arranging or validating objects distance. Increase loop number in such case.

settings.name: skirt_distance
settings.label: Skirt distance
settings.explanation: The distance from the skirt to the brim or the object.

settings.name: skirt_start_angle
settings.label: Skirt start point
settings.explanation: Angle from the object center to skirt start point. Zero is the most right position, counter clockwise is positive angle.

settings.name: skirt_speed
settings.label: Skirt speed
settings.explanation: Speed of skirt, in mm/s. Zero means use default layer extrusion speed.

settings.name: skirt_height
settings.label: Skirt height
settings.explanation: How many layers of skirt. Usually only one layer.

settings.name: draft_shield
settings.label: Draft shield
settings.explanation:
A draft shield is useful to protect an ABS or ASA print from warping and detaching from print bed due to wind draft. It is usually needed only with open frame printers, i.e. without an enclosure.

Enabled = skirt is as tall as the highest printed object. Otherwise 'Skirt height' is used.
Note: With the draft shield active, the skirt will be printed at skirt distance from the object. Therefore, if brims are active it may intersect with them. To avoid this, increase the skirt distance value.

settings.name: single_loop_draft_shield
settings.label: Single loop after first layer
settings.explanation: Limits the skirt/draft shield loops to one wall after the first layer. This is useful, on occasion, to conserve filament but may cause the draft shield/skirt to warp / crack.

settings.name: brim_type
settings.label: Brim type
settings.explanation: This controls the generation of the brim at outer and/or inner side of models. Auto means the brim width is analyzed and calculated automatically.

settings.name: brim_width
settings.label: Brim width
settings.explanation: Distance from model to the outermost brim line.

settings.name: brim_object_gap
settings.label: Brim-object gap
settings.explanation: A gap between innermost brim line and object can make brim be removed more easily.

settings.name: brim_flow_ratio
settings.label: Brim flow ratio
settings.explanation:
This factor affects the amount of material for brims.

The actual brim flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

Note: The resulting value will not be affected by the first-layer flow ratio.

settings.name: brim_use_efc_outline
settings.label: Brim follows compensated outline
settings.explanation:
When enabled, the brim is aligned with the first-layer perimeter geometry after Elephant Foot Compensation is applied.
This option is intended for cases where Elephant Foot Compensation significantly alters the first-layer footprint.

If your current setup already works well, enabling it may be unnecessary and can cause the brim to fuse with upper layers.

settings.name: combine_brims
settings.label: Combine brims
settings.explanation: Combine multiple brims into one when they are close to each other. This can improve brim adhesion.

settings.name: brim_ears_max_angle
settings.label: Brim ear max angle
settings.explanation:
Maximum angle to let a brim ear appear.
If set to 0, no brim will be created.
If set to ~180, brim will be created on everything but straight sections.

settings.name: brim_ears_detection_length
settings.label: Brim ear detection radius
settings.explanation:
The geometry will be decimated before detecting sharp angles. This parameter indicates the minimum length of the deviation for the decimation.
0 to deactivate.

settings.name: slicing_mode
settings.label: Slicing Mode
settings.explanation: Use "Even-odd" for 3DLabPrint airplane models. Use "Close holes" to close all holes in the model.

settings.name: print_sequence
settings.label: Print sequence
settings.explanation: Print sequence, layer by layer or object by object.

settings.name: print_order
settings.label: Intra-layer order
settings.explanation: Print order within a single layer.

settings.name: spiral_mode
settings.label: Spiral vase
settings.explanation: Spiralize smooths out the Z moves of the outer contour. And turns a solid model into a single walled print with solid bottom layers. The final generated model has no seam.

settings.name: spiral_mode_smooth
settings.label: Smooth Spiral
settings.explanation: Smooth Spiral smooths out X and Y moves as well, resulting in no visible seam at all, even in the XY directions on walls that are not vertical.

settings.name: spiral_mode_max_xy_smoothing
settings.label: Max XY Smoothing
settings.explanation: Maximum distance to move points in XY to try to achieve a smooth spiral. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

settings.name: spiral_starting_flow_ratio
settings.label: Spiral starting flow ratio
settings.explanation: Sets the starting flow ratio while transitioning from the last bottom layer to the spiral. Normally the spiral transition scales the flow ratio from 0% to 100% during the first loop which can in some cases lead to under extrusion at the start of the spiral.

settings.name: spiral_finishing_flow_ratio
settings.label: Spiral finishing flow ratio
settings.explanation: Sets the finishing flow ratio while ending the spiral. Normally the spiral transition scales the flow ratio from 100% to 0% during the last loop which can in some cases lead to under extrusion at the end of the spiral.

settings.name: timelapse_type
settings.label: Timelapse
settings.explanation: If smooth or traditional mode is selected, a timelapse video will be generated for each print. After each layer is printed, a snapshot is taken with the chamber camera. All of these snapshots are composed into a timelapse video when printing completes. If smooth mode is selected, the toolhead will move to the excess chute after each layer is printed and then take a snapshot. Since the melt filament may leak from the nozzle during the process of taking a snapshot, a prime tower is required for smooth mode to wipe nozzle.

settings.name: enable_wrapping_detection
settings.label: Enable clumping detection
settings.explanation: Enable clumping detection

settings.name: fuzzy_skin
settings.label: Fuzzy Skin
settings.explanation: Randomly jitter while printing the wall, so that the surface has a rough look. This setting controls the fuzzy position.

settings.name: fuzzy_skin_mode
settings.label: Fuzzy skin generator mode
settings.explanation:
Fuzzy skin generation mode. Works only with Arachne!
Displacement: Сlassic mode when the pattern is formed by shifting the nozzle sideways from the original path.
Extrusion: The mode when the pattern formed by the amount of extruded plastic. This is the fast and straight algorithm without unnecessary nozzle shake that gives a smooth pattern. But it is more useful for forming loose walls in the entire they array.
Combined: Joint mode [Displacement] + [Extrusion]. The appearance of the walls is similar to [Displacement] Mode, but it leaves no pores between the perimeters.

Attention! The [Extrusion] and [Combined] modes works only the fuzzy_skin_thickness parameter not more than the thickness of printed loop. At the same time, the width of the extrusion for a particular layer should also not be below a certain level. It is usually equal 15-25%% of a layer height. Therefore, the maximum fuzzy skin thickness with a perimeter width of 0.4 mm and a layer height of 0.2 mm will be 0.4-(0.2*0.25)=±0.35mm! If you enter a higher parameter than this, the error Flow::spacing() will displayed, and the model will not be sliced. You can choose this number until this error is repeated.

settings.name: fuzzy_skin_noise_type
settings.label: Fuzzy skin noise type
settings.explanation:
Noise type to use for fuzzy skin generation:
Classic: Classic uniform random noise.
Perlin: Perlin noise, which gives a more consistent texture.
Billow: Similar to perlin noise, but clumpier.
Ridged Multifractal: Ridged noise with sharp, jagged features. Creates marble-like textures.
Voronoi: Divides the surface into voronoi cells, and displaces each one by a random amount. Creates a patchwork texture.
Ripple: Uniform ripple pattern that ripples left and right of the original path. Repeating pattern, woven appearance.

settings.name: fuzzy_skin_point_distance
settings.label: Fuzzy skin point distance
settings.explanation: The average distance between the random points introduced on each line segment.

settings.name: fuzzy_skin_thickness
settings.label: Fuzzy skin thickness
settings.explanation: The width within which to jitter. It's advised to be below outer wall line width.

settings.name: fuzzy_skin_scale
settings.label: Fuzzy skin feature size
settings.explanation: The base size of the coherent noise features, in mm. Higher values will result in larger features.

settings.name: fuzzy_skin_octaves
settings.label: Fuzzy Skin Noise Octaves
settings.explanation: The number of octaves of coherent noise to use. Higher values increase the detail of the noise, but also increase computation time.

settings.name: fuzzy_skin_persistence
settings.label: Fuzzy skin noise persistence
settings.explanation: The decay rate for higher octaves of the coherent noise. Lower values will result in smoother noise.

settings.name: fuzzy_skin_ripples_per_layer
settings.label: Number of ripples per layer
settings.explanation: Controls how many full cycles of ripples will be added per layer.

settings.name: fuzzy_skin_ripple_offset
settings.label: Ripple offset
settings.explanation:
Shifts the ripple phase forward along the print path by the specified percentage of a wavelength each layer period.
- 0% keeps every layer identical.
- 50% shifts the pattern by half a wavelength, effectively inverting the phase.
- 100% shifts the pattern by a full wavelength, returning to the original phase.

The shift is applied once every number of layers set by Layers between ripple offset, so layers within the same group are printed identically.

settings.name: fuzzy_skin_layers_between_ripple_offset
settings.label: Layers between ripple offset
settings.explanation:
Specifies how many consecutive layers share the same ripple phase before the offset is applied.
For example:
- 1 = Layer 1 is printed with the base ripple pattern, then layer 2 is shifted by the configured offset, then layer 3 returns to the base pattern, and so on.
- 3 = Layers 1 to 3 are printed with the base ripple pattern, then layers 4 to 6 are shifted by the configured offset, then layers 7 to 9 return to the base pattern, etc.

settings.name: fuzzy_skin_first_layer
settings.label: Apply fuzzy skin to first layer
settings.explanation: Whether to apply fuzzy skin on the first layer.

settings.name: reduce_infill_retraction
settings.label: Reduce infill retraction
settings.explanation: Don't retract when the travel is entirely within an infill area. That means the oozing can't been seen. This can reduce times of retraction for complex model and save printing time, but make slicing and G-code generating slower. Note that z-hop is also not performed in areas where retraction is skipped.

settings.name: gcode_add_line_number
settings.label: Add line number
settings.explanation: Enable this to add line number(Nx) at the beginning of each G-code line.

settings.name: gcode_comments
settings.label: Verbose G-code
settings.explanation: Enable this to get a commented G-code file, with each line explained by a descriptive text. If you print from SD card, the additional weight of the file could make your firmware slow down.

settings.name: gcode_label_objects
settings.label: Label objects
settings.explanation: Enable this to add comments into the G-code labeling print moves with what object they belong to, which is useful for the Octoprint CancelObject plug-in. This setting is NOT compatible with Single Extruder Multi Material setup and Wipe into Object / Wipe into Infill.

settings.name: exclude_object
settings.label: Exclude objects
settings.explanation: Enable this option to add EXCLUDE OBJECT command in G-code.

settings.name: notes
settings.label: Configuration notes
settings.explanation: You can put here your personal notes. This text will be added to the G-code header comments.
